Defendant No. 2 contested the suit, by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, that, the suit land along with other lands measuring 0.26 acre originally belonged to Ghetu Pramanik in 8 annas share, Horibhokta Pramanik in 4 annas share and Tenu Pramanik in 4 annas share; that on the basis of amicable partition, Ghetu Pramanik became the owner of 0.26 acre of land and as such while possessing the same, Ghetu Pramanik died leaving behind three sons namely Juran, Hridoy and Kurani as his heirs; thereafter Hridoy died leaving behind his son Nitai and Kurani died leaving behind his daughter Monisha; that Juran Mondal by amicable partition had been possessing the entire 0.26 acre of land out of which he transferred 0,13 acre along with 0.38 acre in RS Plot no. 219, 0.6 'A acre in RS Plot No. 185 and 0.38k acre in RS Plot No. 186 of Binodpur Boroldwido mouza in total .96 acre of land to Haider Mondal by registered kabala dated 23.02.1956; that Haider Mondal died leaving behind two sons namely, Kutu Mondal and Dudu Mondal and they transferred .15 acre, of the suit land along with acre out of .37 acre of land in SA Plot No. 185 and 0.45½ acre out of 0.88 acre of land in SA Plot No. 186, totalling .70 acre of land to defendant No.2; that the said defendant No.2 although purchased 0.15 acre of the suit land but he possessed the entire 0.26 acre of the suit land; that thereafter the defendant no.2 on 09.10.1986 transferred 0.15 acre; of land out of the suit land along with .11¼ acre of land from Plots no. 185 and 186 in total .26¼ acre of land to the plaintiffs and the defendant No.1; that the defendant no.1 obtained 0.10 acre of land in the western part of the suit land; that pursuant to amicable settlement RS record has been prepared and accordingly he is possessing the same upon erecting houses thereon; that the defendant No.2 is the owner and possessor of 0.08 acre of land situated in the eastern side adjacent to the 0.10 acre of land of the defendant No.1 on the western side which has been recorded in the RS record in his name; that on the basis of settlement the plaintiffs are possessing 0.08 acre on the eastern side of the suit land along with 0.09 acre of land in SA Plot No. 185 in total .17 acre of land which has been recorded in his name; that the RS record has not been prepared in the name of the defendant no.2; that the plain-tiff no.1 fraudulently got .44 acre of land of defendant no.2 in Plot no. 186 recorded in his name in RS Khatian No. 517, Plots No. 345 and 346 and erected some houses in some portion of the same forcibly and dispossessed the defendants; that the plaintiff no.1 expressed about the purchase of .10 acre of land from Nitai and Monisha on 18.11.1972 but had no possession over the same; that Ni tai Left for India during Pakistan regime; that the plaintiffs on false personation fraudulently created the deed by which no title vested upon him and, as such, the suit is not maintainable; hence the suit should be dismissed. 

 18. In the case of Syed Abdul Haque Vs. Surendra. Nath Majumder, reported in 59 DLR(AD) 111 this Division held "since the documents exhibits 1 and 2 are 30 years old and have a presumption of correctness and that presumption having not been dislodged by the defendants there was no occasion for the Court to discard the claim of title of the plaintiffs made on the basis of the said documents." This Division in the case of Bangladesh Railway Vs. Jashimuddin, reported in 5 LM(AD)58 held. "from- the discussions made herein above since the plaintiffs have been successful in proving their genealogy of title and possession in the suit land and since the defendants failed to challenge the documents relied upon by the plaintiffs and also failed to prove their case of title and possession, it can clearly be held that the defendants have no title and possession in the suit land. On the other hand the plaintiffs could prove the title of Yeasin Hazi, the CS recorded tenant and thereafter devolution of title and possession upon his daughter Duburunnessa who in her turn transferred the same to Khodeza Begum by two registered documents in 1955 and 1956 which are more than 30 years old documents and relying on such registered documents Khodeza Begum's name being recorded in the SA record and thereafter Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs having purchased the same got his name mutated in place of Khodeza Begum in the office of the Government, and after his death his heirs, the plaintiffs having got, their names mutated, the title and possession of the plaintiffs are found to be proved".
